    The recursive resolver does the searching on the client's behalf and caches the answers. If its cache               
    misses, it starts at the root of the DNS hierarchy. It already knows the addresses of the root servers.             
    It asks a root server for example.com. The root does not hold the final address. It answers with a                  
    referral to the servers responsible for the .com zone, the top-level domain.                                        
                                                                                                                        
    The resolver then queries a .com server. That server also replies with a referral, this time to the                 
    authoritative name servers for example.com, whose names and addresses are published in the parent zone.             
    The resolver queries one of those authoritative servers. That server holds the zone data and returns                
    the record that was requested. For ordinary web access this is usually an A record with an IPv4 address             
    or an AAAA record with an IPv6 address. The response includes a time to live, or TTL, which says how                
    many seconds the answer may be cached.                                                                              
                                                                                                                        
    The recursive resolver stores the record, returns it to the stub, and the application can connect.                  
    Later lookups for the same name skip the full walk until the TTL expires. A name may also point                     
    elsewhere first. A CNAME record aliases one name to another, and the resolver follows that chain until              
    it reaches address records. Reverse lookups invert the process, mapping an address back to a name                   
    through special in-addr.arpa or ip6.arpa zones.                                                                     
                                                                                                                        
    Resolution is mostly a sequence of cached referrals from root to TLD to authoritative server, ending in             
    one or more address records the client can use.                                                                     
                                                                                                                        
    Worked for 12s
